title: Kaja Kallas Appointed EU Foreign Policy Chief
reason: Kaja Kallas was nominated as EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy on 28 June 2024, confirmed by the European Parliament in November 2024, and took office on 1 December 2024. She resigned as prime minister to take up the role. Confirmed by the European Council, EU Commission, and Estonian government.

title: Kristen Michal Becomes Prime Minister
reason: Kristen Michal of the Reform Party was nominated on 29 June 2024 and sworn in as prime minister on 23 July 2024, succeeding Kaja Kallas. His cabinet includes ministers from the Reform Party, Social Democrats, and Estonia 200. Confirmed by Wikipedia, ERR, and the Estonian government website.

title: Parliament Revokes Local Voting Rights for Non-Citizens
reason: On 26 March 2025, the Riigikogu approved constitutional amendments revoking local election voting rights for third-country nationals (primarily targeting Russian and Belarusian citizens) with 92 MPs in favour. The amendments take effect for the October 2025 local elections, confirmed by the Riigikogu, Library of Congress, and IDEA Democracy Tracker.
